title: Calculate an 18% tip
concept: 18% is one of the most common tip amounts — but it's awkward because it's not a round number. The trick is to never try to calculate 18% in one step.
shortcut: Find 10% by moving the decimal one place left. Take half of that for 5%. Add a small 3% bump (roughly 30 cents per $10). Or skip the math entirely: double the tax line on your receipt — in most US states that's close to 18%.

title: The 10% trick
concept: 10% is the foundation of all tip math. Moving the decimal one place left gives you 10% of any number instantly. From there you can build any tip in seconds.
shortcut: 10% of $65 = $6.50 (just move the decimal). Double it for 20% = $13.00. Add half for 15% = $9.75. Master this one move and every tip becomes a two-second calculation.

title: Split the bill right
concept: Always add the tip to the full bill before splitting. If you split first then tip separately, each person tips on a smaller amount and the server gets shortchanged.
shortcut: The right order: Total → add tip → divide by people. A $80 bill with 20% tip becomes $96 total. Split 4 ways: $24 each. Never divide first — you lose cents in rounding and everyone underpays.

title: The 25% shortcut
concept: 25% off means you pay 75% of the original price. Since 25% equals one quarter (¼), you can find the discount instantly by dividing the price by 4.
shortcut: Divide by 4 to find 25% of any price. That's your savings. Subtract from original to get the sale price. For 50% off, divide by 2. For 10% off, just move the decimal.

title: 10% off — the gateway discount
concept: 10% is the foundation of all discount math. It's the easiest percentage to calculate: just move the decimal point one place to the left. Every other discount — 20%, 25%, 30% — is built from this single move.
shortcut: Move the decimal left to find 10%. $80 → $8 off. $120 → $12 off. For 20% off, double that number. For 5% off, halve it. This one move unlocks every discount on any price tag.

title: Buy 2 get 1 free — the real math
concept: "Buy 2 get 1 free" is 33% off, not 50%. You pay for 2 items and receive 3. The free item's cost is spread across all three, so each item effectively costs two-thirds of the full price.
shortcut: Per-item cost = (2 × full price) ÷ 3. Total saving = 1 full item's price. For $9 shampoo: pay $18 for 3 → $6 per bottle, save $9 total. Ask: do you actually need all 3?
example:
Shampoo: $9.00 each
Buy 2 get 1 free
You pay: $18.00 for 3
Per bottle = $6.00
Total saving = $9.00

title: Stacking discounts
concept: Two discounts stacked together don't simply add up. 20% off plus 10% off is NOT 30% off — the second discount applies to the already-reduced price. You always save a little less than the sum suggests.
shortcut: Apply discounts one at a time. $100 → 20% off → $80 → 10% off $80 → $72. Saving: $28, not $30. Quick rule: each 10% combo loses about 1% to stacking. Two 50%-off coupons would only be 75% off, not 100%.

title: Compare unit prices
concept: Bigger packs look cheaper, but they're not always cheaper per item. Divide the total price by the number of items to find the unit price — the true cost of one — so you can make a fair comparison.
shortcut: Unit price = total price ÷ quantity. 6-pack for $7.20 → $7.20 ÷ 6 = $1.20 each. Singles at $1.49? The pack wins. Always check before you grab the bigger size — it's not always the better deal.
example:
6-pack: $7.20
÷ 6 items = $1.20 each
Singles: $1.49 each
Pack saves: $0.29 per item

title: Add sales tax in your head
concept: Sales tax is usually 6–10% depending on your state. Since it's close to 10%, use 10% as your anchor and nudge down. You'll be within cents every time.
shortcut: For 8% tax: find 10% (move the decimal left), then subtract 20% of that. On a $40 item: 10% = $4.00, minus $0.80 = $3.20 tax. Total = $43.20. Rounding up to 10% and ignoring the rest works fine for budgeting.

title: Estimate your cart total
concept: You don't need exact prices to stay on budget. Round each item to the nearest dollar as you shop, keep a running mental sum, and you'll hit the register knowing you're covered.
shortcut: Round every item up: $3.79 → $4, $8.49 → $9, $1.19 → $2. Add the rounded numbers. Your estimate will land a dollar or two above the actual total — exactly the right direction for budgeting. Never try to track cents.

title: Double and half in a second
concept: Doubling and halving are the fastest mental operations you have. They're the foundation of 200% increases, 50% off deals, splitting bills, and finding midpoints. Speed up by splitting numbers into round parts.
shortcut: To double $37: split into $30 + $7, double each ($60 + $14), add for $74. To halve: even numbers are instant. Odd: subtract 1, halve, add $0.50. $37 ÷ 2 = $18.50.

title: Multiply by 5 the fast way
concept: Multiplying by 5 looks hard but it's just ×10 then ÷2. Since finding 10% is automatic (move the decimal), you already know the hard part. One extra halving step and you're done.
shortcut: $46 × 5: move decimal → $460, halve → $230. Works for any number. In reverse: ÷5 means ÷10 then ×2. Useful for per-item pricing, hourly rates, and 5-pack deals.
